quotes.text: Build an integration where you render the Payment Element before you create a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent, then confirm the Intent from your server.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: You can use the ConfirmationToken sent by your client to create and confirm the PaymentIntent in a single request.
To set up a payment method for future payments, you must attach it to an object that represents your customer.

findings: Semantic raw delta: November raw lines 5-15 retain the common deferred-Element/server-confirm identity and expose three web variant URLs, while May old raw lines 8-734, 734-1570 and 1571-2541 contain detailed payment, setup and subscription flows. Diff lines 1-13 and 2542-2544 show a combined guide replaced by an index, not evidence that detailed behavior was deprecated or newly changed.

Existing summary baseline accuracy: source lines 13-30 reasonably describe the May payment variant, but source lines 32-34 call setup 'Same' without the May requirement to attach the method to a customer-configured Account or Customer (old raw lines 1118-1128), and the source lacks the subscription variant, whose example creates a default_incomplete Subscription and separately confirms its invoice PaymentIntent (old raw lines 2446-2490). Both variants are explicitly discoverable in new raw lines 14-15.

The May payment variant uses client Elements mode/amount/currency and paymentMethodCreation manual, elements.submit and createConfirmationToken, then server trusted amount and PaymentIntent create/confirm (old raw lines 82-103, 455-465, 491-536, 647-675). The SetupIntent is distinct from payment and must not imply a charge (old raw lines 734-738, 1374-1402). New raw lines 7-15 do not refresh those detailed instructions.

May outcome boundary: requires_action calls for client handleNextAction, and payment_intent.succeeded events should drive post-payment work rather than a client callback (old raw lines 689-720). The source line 30 mentions next action but not reliable completion; the new raw lines 7-15 establish no succeeded state or transaction outcome.

Main route exists: root wiki/index.md line 7 routes to wiki/stripe-index.md lines 558 and 729, then wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-intents.md lines 43-48 and 145-148 routes the current source. Source lines 46-48 preserve the May raw link, but the November index raw is not represented.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May 11, 2026 payment-flow details dated: manual Payment Element configuration, 12-hour unused ConfirmationToken expiry, server PaymentIntent create/confirm and client next-action handling (old raw lines 82-103, 455-465, 635-720; current source lines 13-30).

Keep May setup prerequisites and outcome distinct: customer-configured Account or Customer attachment, SetupIntent confirmation, and separate later off-session PaymentIntent with possible 402/authentication-required failure (old raw lines 1118-1128, 1374-1537).

Keep May subscription path distinct: recurring Price and customer prerequisites, immediate-charge amount or trial zero, invoice settings consistency, default_incomplete Subscription then latest-invoice PaymentIntent confirmation (old raw lines 1592-1598, 1647-1658, 2024-2028, 2163-2165, 2446-2490).
The seven SDK minimum versions in source lines 36-38 come from the dated May payment section old raw lines 635-645; the November index gives no version update.
conflicts: The May example returns client_secret/status in old raw lines 673-676 yet its handleNextAction example accesses response.clientSecret in old raw lines 699-703 (also setup old raw lines 1399-1402 versus 1425-1429). Treat this as an example naming inconsistency, not demonstrated runtime behavior; current source lines 29-30 reproduce the mismatch and need a narrow warning or consistent conceptual wording.

Current source lines 19-22 present a broad deferred-versus-server comparison; the May server variant examples use paymentMethodCreation manual (old raw lines 86-103), while the general Elements options table labels it optional (old raw lines 428-453). Scope the setting to the shown variant rather than a universal Stripe.js requirement.
unresolved_questions: The November index points to three variant URLs (new raw lines 13-15) but their 2026-11-07 detailed contents were not pinned here; any current variant behavior, SDK minimum or availability change needs separately authorized capture.

findings: Add the 2026-11-07 raw as a navigation-only capture and retain the 2026-05-11 guide as dated implementation authority (new raw lines 7-15; old raw lines 1-12; current source lines 4-8, 46-48).

Repair baseline coverage: source lines 32-34 flatten SetupIntent prerequisites and omit the subscription branch, although old raw lines 1118-1128 and 2446-2490 distinguish them and new raw lines 14-15 route to them.
Qualify next-action and completion boundaries using old raw lines 689-720; avoid claiming the new index proves successful payments.
conflicts: May sample response field client_secret at old raw lines 673-676 conflicts with response.clientSecret at old raw lines 699-703; current source lines 29-30 echo both spellings.

The old raw lines 428-453 optional Elements table and payment variant old raw lines 86-103 support a variant-specific manual setting, not a universal rule; current source lines 17-22 risk overgeneralization.
source_assessments.reason: The raw delta is navigation-only, but the current summary has material baseline omissions and an example-field mismatch; a dated dual-raw source update is needed to preserve routes and prevent wrong setup/subscription implementation selection.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/finalize-payments-on-the-server, the complete November capture says to render the Payment Element before creating a PaymentIntent or SetupIntent and confirm the Intent on the server; it then routes web payment, setup, and subscription variants (new raw lines 5-15). The May guide provides the dated implementation: payment uses client submit and ConfirmationToken, a server-owned amount and PaymentIntent create/confirm, and client handling of requires_action (old raw lines 455-465 and 647-720). Setup uses a SetupIntent attached to a customer-configured Account or Customer, without an immediate charge (old raw lines 734-738 and 1118-1128). Subscription uses a Price/customer and a default_incomplete Subscription followed by invoice PaymentIntent confirmation (old raw lines 2446-2490). The mapped source-stripe-finalize-payments-server.md summarizes payment but flattens setup and omits subscription (current source lines 13-38); neither capture proves successful execution or funds availability.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/finalize-payments-on-the-server, the November replacement is an index and variant-navigation change, with no demonstrated substantive payment-flow change (new raw lines 7-15; old raw lines 8-12 and 1571-1575; diff lines 1-13 and 2542-2544). source-stripe-finalize-payments-server.md must keep its May 11, 2026 ConfirmationToken, SDK minima and next-action claims dated while adding the November raw route and repairing the setup/subscription coverage (current source lines 4-8, 26-38, 46-48). May examples disagree on client_secret versus clientSecret (old raw lines 673-703); this needs a warning, not a fabricated API change. The web/Stripe.js variant's manual Elements setting and server confirmation do not establish universal client SDK behavior, current variant availability, payment success or fulfillment; May explicitly favors payment_intent.succeeded event handling (old raw lines 82-103 and 689-720).
